verdict: Caution: lend selectively to integrated, ethanol-linked mills and their cane suppliers with clean payment records; avoid standalone mills with cane-arrears and wage disputes.
title: Kashipur Sugar & Ethanol: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A sugar mill crushes cane within hours of harvest, so the whole model is a race against sucrose loss: cane in, sugar and molasses out, ethanol if a distillery is attached. **Cash is made in the crush season and consumed in the off-season, so the working-capital cycle, not the P&L, decides survival.** Cane is bought at a state-administered price, sugar is sold at market, and ethanol is sold at administered prices [10] — so pricing power sits with the government on both ends and the mill lives on the spread. Capex is lumpy: one peer spent about Rs. 70 crore in FY2024 on refining capacity, funded from internal accruals, lifting realisations by roughly Rs. 0.5–1.0/kg [9].

## What has changed in Kashipur now
Local reporting is thin, so lean on first principles plus peers. **The live local signal is a labour dispute at the Bajpur mill over cane allocation and revised pay [1], and farmers say they will expand cane area only if cane dues are paid on time [2][3].** That is the classic arrears spiral: late payment shrinks next year's cane, which cuts crush, which worsens payment. The state backdrop is weak — Uttarakhand GST collections are -19.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D], and electricity demand is +4.7% against India +9.5% [D]. Nationally, bank credit is -7.0% YoY against output +5.1% [D]. Peer results are better than the local picture: Triveni reports improved profitability and reduced debt on strong sugar and distillery margins [5], and EID Parry lifted realisations to INR 51.2/kg from INR 43.7/kg [6]. Rating commentary says ethanol prices and interest subvention should prevent cane arrears piling up for integrated mills [10].

## Where to grow
**Pursue integrated mills with a working distillery and a clean cane-payment record, and the cane suppliers and transporters tied to them.** Ethanol-linked cash flow is the growth engine [10]. Avoid standalone mills with arrears, and avoid any proposal where the promoter cannot show the last crush season's payment dates — collect from customer.

## How to grow safely
Structure against the season, not the year: **cash-flow-backed limits sized to one crush cycle, with a cane-payment escrow and monthly stock-and-receivables statements.** Take monthly: cane dues paid versus received, sugar and ethanol stock, and distillery run-rate. If a proposal lands, check the arrears ageing; if dues exceed one season, ask for the state subsidy or ethanol receivables as security.

## Early-warning signs
- Monthly cane-dues ageing (monthly): arrears cross one season -> freeze fresh limits.
- Wage/gate-meeting reports (monthly): repeat protests [1] -> reassess crush continuity.
- Distillery utilisation (monthly): falls below plan -> shift to secured receivables lending.
- State GST trend (monthly) [D]: stays negative -> tighten new-to-bank.
